failures.criterion: Architect's direction for this round (envoy e436ee03): Go's refusal of a footnote definition inside a typed block must not misstate the browser editor's behaviour
failures.evidence:
At head, pmdoc refusals.go:83 refuses `Ref[^1].

:::callout{#c1 kind="note" title="T"}
[^1]: x
:::
` with 'which the browser editor refers to only from inside a typed block or after it' (parse_test.go:78-81 states the same). The headless engine at head, read-only and default, reads both rows of parse_test.go:87-88 as paragraph+footnote_reference with the definition inside the callout (the quote row likewise) and serializes each back byte for byte, the same tree it reads for a definition inside a quote, which Go accepts. With lines 82-84 of refusals.go removed (temporary, restored), Go reads both rows to that same tree and renders them back as written, and TestParseMatchesMilkdownForFixtures still passes. So no reason about the browser holds: the corrected behaviour is to read the definition as the browser does. Red test: TestParseReadsAFootnoteDefinitionInsideATypedBlockAsTheBrowserDoes in packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/pmdoc/parse_test.go (commit b5d904f9). Fails now: `cd packages/envoy && go test -count=1 -run TestParseReadsAFootnoteDefinitionInsideATypedBlockAsTheBrowserDoes ./internal/dispatch/pmdoc/` -> 'outside Proof schema: a footnote definition inside a typed block, which the browser editor refers to only from inside a typed block or after it, want it read as the browser editor reads it' for both rows. Passes with the refusal removed. The two typed-block rows of TestParseRefusesAFootnoteDefinitionInsideAnotherOrATypedBlock (parse_test.go:87-88) and its doc comment pin the old behaviour and go with the fix.

observations: Nesting cost at the bound, headless warm best of 3: 32 unclosed `:::a` then 32,000-char bodies cost 1.6x (x lines), 1.55x (list items), 2.1x (quote lines), 3.4x (blank-separated paragraphs: 4.1 s vs 1.2 s) the same body with no `:::`; in Chromium the blank-separated body took 3,519 ms against 2,115 ms with no `:::` (1.66x). Linear and bounded as the plan says; the plan's 'at most about 1.6x' holds in the browser but not for every shape headless.

The default mode counts an unknown `:::foo` wrapper toward the 32 bound and refuses line 33 before naming the unknown block; it calls such a wrapper an 'unknown typed block' itself, and Go refuses the same document, so no finding.
